speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: My apologies to Minister of State Alvin Tan.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: He looked so keen to move the Second Reading of his Bill.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I wish to let him know it might be some time before he gets that pleasure.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is not the first time you have presided over the Budget process, having done so in previous years as a Deputy Speaker.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But this is the first time that you have done so as Speaker of the House.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: You ran a tight ship, keeping close control over the process, yet allowing flexibility when needed.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Every year, one Ministry will emerge as the "favourite" with the most number of cuts, even though this is one prize Ministries prefer not to win as it means even more work for the relevant Ministers and their team.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But anyway, for the record, this year, the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) was "the 1" to win the prize and as we know "All Too Well" now, they rose to the occasion with "Style".

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Members may not quite get the references I just made, but it is alright, if you ask your children or Ms Usha, they will know.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Budget 2023 was delivered on 14 February and is remembered as a Valentine's Day Budget, especially with its family-oriented measures.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This year's Budget was delivered on 16 February, which coincidentally fell on the seventh day of the first month in the traditional Chinese calendar, also known as “Ren Ri” or Everyman's Birthday.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is fortuitous since Budget 2024 is a Budget with something for everyone – so, everyone got a birthday present under Budget 2024!

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: More importantly, Budget 2024 gives life and breath to the plans in the Forward Singapore report that we, as Singaporeans, collectively developed to build our shared future together.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Budgets 2020-2023 helped us to get through the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Those Budgets, including five Budgets in 2020 alone, helped save lives, save jobs and enabled us to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But the post-pandemic world into which we emerged is very different from the one from which we entered.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The world in which Budget 2024 takes place is messier, more dangerous and more unpredictable.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In Gaza and Ukraine, there has been the tragic loss of life.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Even though these are far away, in an interconnected world, we are not unaffected.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As a small nation-state, we have to navigate an increasingly fragmented world order fraught with geopolitical contestation.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Climate change poses an existential threat for us given our small size, low-lying land and energy constraints.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At a more personal and individual level, Singaporeans remain concerned with costs of living and inflationary pressures and other immediate concerns.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Against this backdrop, Budget 2024 provides a clear action plan to take Singapore forward into the future with optimism and hope, these challenges notwithstanding.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Budget 2024 also sets aside resources for policies that will allow us to turn challenges into opportunities, reinvigorate our workforce by helping workers find new paths and second careers and build a Singapore that is vibrant and inclusive, fair and thriving, resilient and united.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, let me recap what we have set in motion by approving this Budget.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also took decisive measures to ensure a strong, innovative and vibrant economy.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: To maintain our competitive edge and ride the winds of change, we amped up support for our National Artificial Intelligence (AI) Strategy 2.0.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this connection, I should mention that Dr Tan Wu Meng's speech on this topic, which took us on a masterful tour of the rapid AI advancements and how we prepare our citizens for this change, has attracted global attention.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The clip of his post has garnered several million views across various platforms.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is a good example showing how, although we are a small Parliament, what we say and do in this House can be noticed far beyond our shores.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: So, I encourage Members to keep up the quality of our debates and thereby the credibility of this House.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We introduced the Refundable Investment Credit to enhance our investment promotion toolkit, as global competition for investments intensifies with BEPS 2.0.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The new SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme – which includes the top-up in SkillsFuture Credits for Singaporeans aged 40 and above to pursue selected training programmes, the new SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance and the opportunity to pursue another full-time diploma – are all intended to empower Singaporeans throughout their journey of lifelong learning so that they can continue to access opportunities at every stage of life, for every stage of life.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Many of these moves were informed by ground-up feedback from citizens through the Forward Singapore exercise.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These measures give effect to Singaporeans' wishes to upgrade their skills and seize new opportunities and help them embrace a culture of lifelong learning.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By respecting and rewarding every job, we hope that these initiatives will enhance opportunities across diverse pathways and enable all Singaporeans to progress throughout their careers.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We further strengthened our social compact by providing more support to those who need it the most.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The ComLink+ Progress Packages will uphold social mobility and ensure that families from all backgrounds will have access to full and fair opportunities.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also strengthened access to justice, especially for the most vulnerable, through the civil and criminal law systems.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Families are the bedrock of our society and we have committed to supporting them through every stage of life – from providing strong foundations for the young, to enhancing the golden years of the elderly.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The pilot to provide affordable and reliable childminding services will give parents another caregiving option and hopefully pave the way for such services to be delivered at greater scale.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For our seniors, we have made adjustments to the Central Provident Fund system and strengthened the Silver Support Scheme to support their retirement needs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Young seniors will get an additional boost for their retirement through the Majulah Package.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We also set aside funds for Age Well SG, a new national programme to support seniors to age actively, stay socially connected and be cared for in their own communities.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These initiatives position us well to holistically take care of the needs of our ageing society.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Inclusivity is the glue on which unity is built.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: By building on the previous Budgets and having something for everyone, Budget 2024 ensures that no one is left behind.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: At the same time, by creating opportunities and providing catalytic assistance to encourage and amplify individual effort, we are fostering a resilient and united Singapore.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On behalf of the House, I would also like to convey our appreciation to the Clerk of Parliament, Deputy Clerk and the other Assistant Clerks, as well as the Parliament Secretariat and staff, interpreters and translators, whose dedicated efforts and support behind the scenes over the past two weeks ensured that the proceedings went smoothly.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Unlike Members of Parliament (MPs) who are seen and heard on camera, their work is unseen and often unsung.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: But it is only because of what they do that we as MPs can do what we need to do.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Hon Members, it has been a long but intense debate – nine days for Budget 2024, a Budget that moves our country upwards and forward.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting in this Chair and also down there, in that chair, I listened intently and quietly to all of you and, in some cases, we went for a six-hour session before going for a break.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For me, this debate scored a few firsts.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Personally, this is the first Budget and Committee of Supply in which I am Speaker.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Accordingly, it is the first time in 18 years that I did not have to make a Budget speech nor file any cuts.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And for the record, I averaged about 10 cuts per Budget.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In fact, this is the first time in the last six years that there was a decline in the number for cuts over the previous year.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I think, in part, due to the fact that we have fewer Members in the House this year.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: There is one other first which we all do not want.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Singaporeans are very special to all of us and our Budget reflects that from birth to old age.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are spending more than ever on each one.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Being a father myself to two adult children now, I can only hope that more young Singaporeans will have the privilege of experiencing the joy of being parents themselves.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But the next first is something which is a good first.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It is the first time in three years when Members from both sides of the aisle have explicitly expressed their support for the Budget.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And this support came from no less than the leaders of both opposition parties.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We all want to build a Singapore for all and we want to build it for all Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Whether speeches are long or short, whether it is 15 cuts that you filed or five cuts, all I can say is that more is not necessarily better.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: In fact, I also heard Members from both sides of the House echoing the same in that more handouts are not necessarily good.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Likewise, more Parliamentary Questions, more Committees are not necessarily better.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Indeed, from my perspective, crispier and sharper speeches are much preferred and the order for the day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: When speeches go on too long, some of us may start to wonder whether they were written by ChatGPT.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I am glad that there was no need for me to cut anyone off, although there were quite a few Members who breached your time allocations but, in the spirit of give and take, I cut them some slack.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: But please do not take this as a given.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: For those Members who attempted to slip in a mini speech during clarification time, please refrain from doing so, as I will be more strict from now on.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It leaves me now to thank all Members for your cooperation and support in helping me ensure we had a smooth Budget debate.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: My appreciation also goes to the Leader of the House, Minister Indranee Rajah, and also her Deputy, Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: My final round of thanks goes to my two Deputy Speakers, Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Christopher de Souza, my Clerks and all, all the support staff for ensuring that proceedings went well each day throughout the entire two-week period.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: It does take meticulous care, experience and a whole team to ensure Budget and Committee of Supply 2024 went smoothly.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And the Parliament of Singapore has, over the years, received the support from an invaluable and experienced team.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong has described the world we are in now as, I quote, “messier, more dangerous and more unpredictable.” As a small country, we cannot do much to remake the world into a neater, more predictable one.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Nor should we want to, because complexity and multilinearity is a part of the human condition.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: To thrive in this new world, Singapore cannot aim to be a mere “safe space”.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We must, as our forefathers have always done, take risks, accept failure and rise again and say “Majulah!” And in this, Singapore is a beautiful home and a safe harbour, where we will help one another along when we are down.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: And we provide over $130 billion and more a year, to those among us who need it most.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Only in this way, can we move Forward Singapore.
